newsitem.title: BARBADOS: CRICKET-WEST INDIES FIGHT BACK AGAINST INDIA.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-WEST INDIES FIGHT BACK AGAINST INDIA.

text.p: West Indies fought their way back into the third test against India on Sunday, taking three wickets for just 41 runs before lunch on the third day.
India, replying to West Indies' first innings score of 298, were 290 for six at lunch with Mohammad Azharuddin unbeaten on 15 and Anil Kumble on eight.
Resuming at 249 for three, India lost the wickets of Saurav Ganguly (22), Rahul Dravid (78) and Nayan Mongia (one) while adding a mere 41 runs in the two-hour morning session.

After just four runs were scored, Ganguly was first to go in the third over of the day, caught by wicketkeeper Courtney Browne off paceman Mervyn Dillon after adding just one run to his overnight score.
Dravid followed with the total on 273, when he was bowled by fast bowler Ian Bishop. He batted for six hours and 12 minutes, faced 243 balls and struck eight fours.
Mongia was brilliantly caught by Stuart Williams in the covers off Bishop for one.
Bishop has been the most successful bowler with three for 70 off 26 overs.
